case_name: Haji Mumtaz Hussain (Dead) Through L.Rs v State of Uttar Pradesh
respondent:
State of Uttar Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

9 February 2000
Civil Appeal No. 2947 of 1982
The Order of the Court was as follows :
1. The appellant filed a suit for recovery of Rs. 40,000 by way of damages on the ground that he had purchased 171 Shisham trees in the area lying between the rivers Dhimri and Baur at an auction sale conducted by the Agricultural Officer, Colonization Scheme by name Shri J. P. Nathani, DW-6, on 25th May. 1952, for a consideration of Rs. 7,500. That though the entire sale consideration was deposited and the appellant started cutting the Shisham trees within the aforesaid area, he was prevented by the Forest and Colonization Department from removing the remaining trees as well as the chattas of fuel wood. After serving a notice under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure, claiming damages for illegal detention of the trees, which the appellant had purchased and felled, the suit was filed. The suit was resisted
facts: The appellant filed a suit for recovery of Rs. 40,000 by way of damages on the ground that he had purchased 171 Shisham trees in the area lying between the rivers Dhimri and Baur at an auction sale conducted by the Agricultural Officer, Colonization Scheme.

That though the entire sale consideration was deposited and the appellant started cutting the Shisham trees within the aforesaid area, he was prevented by the Forest and Colonization Department from removing the remaining trees as well as the chattas of fuel wood.
After serving a notice under Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure, claiming damages for illegal detention of the trees, which the appellant had purchased and felled, the suit was filed.
issues: Whether the plaintiff was given the contract to fell and take away all the Shisham trees in the area situated between Rivers Dhimri and Baur or whether 171 Shisham trees only were sold to him?

Whether the Forest Department of the defendant stopped the plaintiff from working out the contract given to the plaintiff by Colonization Department and illegally seized and confiscated the timber cut by the plaintiff?
Whether the plaintiff has suffered a loss of Rs. 40,000 as alleged by the wrongful and illegal acts of Forest Department
Whether the plaintiff was obstructed in working out of the contract during the stipulated period.
Whether the suit is time barred?
Whether the notice under Section 80, C.P.C. was invalid?
To what relief is the plaintiff entitled?
Whether the plaintiff exported the entire timber of 171 trees purchased by him as alleged?
Whether the plaintiff left behind any timber on 1st December, 1952, of the trees purchased by him?
Whether the suit was barred by Article 299 as alleged?
petitioner_arguments: The plea raised to resist the claim by the State based on Article 299, to say the least, was immoral.
The State could not have taken sale proceeds of 171 trees and still appropriated a part of the property sold.
Appellant could not be deprived of the property purchased by him without payment of compensation.
court_reasoning: In the face of findings of fact recorded by the trial court that 171 Shisham trees had been purchased by the appellant from the Colonization and Forest Department and he had paid the entire sale consideration for those trees and that he had not cut or felled any other tree besides those 171 Shisham trees nor committed any other default justifying detention of a part of the trees, the High Court was not justified in nonsuiting the plaintiff-appellant.
The State could not have taken sale proceeds of 171 trees and still appropriated a part of the property sold.
holding: We accordingly allow this appeal and set aside the judgment of the High Court and restore that of the trial court.
